claims.text: The AWSx ELB component provides APIs for provisioning Application and Network Load Balancers and integrates with API Gateway, ECS, Lambda, and VPC.
The example load balancer listens on port 80 in the account's per-region default VPC using its public subnets, exposing it to the internet.
Targeting an EC2 instance requires opening ingress to the load balancer (explicitly needed for NLB but not ALB), and the steps as listed.
ALBs automatically open ingress traffic to the ports they listen on, whereas NLBs do not.
The Pulumi AWS provider API docs include LaunchTemplate at /registry/packages/aws/api-docs/ec2/launchtemplate/ and AutoScalingGroup at /registry/packages/aws/api-docs/autoscaling/group/.
In AWSx, passing the load balancer's target group in the ECS task definition's `portMappings` makes AWSx populate the ECS service's load balancer configuration automatically.
The AWSx ECS component (`awsx.ecs` classes) automatically creates the right ingress and egress rules; raw `aws.ecs` requires manual security group management.
The ECS example stack exports a `url` output used with curl to reach the endpoint.
ALBs offer two features that make them more attractive for ECS than NLBs: dynamic host port mapping and path-based routing with priority rules.
Pulumi recommends ALBs for ECS services unless a service requires a feature only available with NLBs.
By default a load balancer is created internet-facing using the VPC's public subnets; setting the `internal` property to `true` makes it private.
Load balancers accept an explicit list of subnets via the `subnets` property (subnet objects) or the `subnetIds` property (subnet IDs).
The `listener` property chooses smart defaults based on whether the listener is created against a load balancer or a target group.
NLBs support protocols TCP, TLS, UDP, TCP_UDP, QUIC, and TCP_QUIC while ALBs support HTTP and HTTPS; NLBs default to TCP and ALBs select HTTP or HTTPS based on port.
AWS docs at rule-action-types.html contain fixed-response-actions and redirect-actions anchors.
AWS documentation page listener-rules.html exists about listener rules.
A target group is automatically created for each listener that doesn't override the default action.
The `deregistrationDelay` range is 0–3600 seconds and the default is 300.
The `slowStart` range is 30–900 seconds or 0 to disable, and it is disabled by default.
Target group `stickiness` is available for ALBs only.
The target group `targetType` values are `instance`, `ip`, `lambda`, and `alb`, default `instance`; IPs must be within the VPC private range, RFC 1918 ranges, or RFC 6598 range (100.64.0.0/10).
The health check `interval` range is 5–300 seconds and the default is 30 seconds.
The health check `healthyThreshold` range is 2–10 and the default is 3.
The health check `unhealthyThreshold` range is 2–10, default 3, and for NLBs it must equal `healthyThreshold`.
The health check `timeout` range is 2–120 seconds; AWS defaults are 6 seconds for HTTP target groups and 10 seconds for HTTPS, TCP, and TLS target groups.
